title: Transfer of Property Principles Governing Agricultural & Urban Land Transfers

content.overview: Agricultural and urban land transfers use the same Transfer of Property Act unless a State law creates a special limit. Ceiling, tenancy and government-land restrictions are State statutes. They do not rewrite section 5. Identify the Act that imposes the limit before applying a general transfer rule.

content.study: The TPA still classifies the transfer.

cases.name: Indore Development Authority v. Manoharlal
cases.facts: The Constitution Bench considered lapse of acquisition proceedings and the interaction of possession and compensation.
cases.issue: How should the statutory lapse provision apply to pending acquisitions?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Lapse depends on the statutory conditions and cannot be established by a unilateral refusal or incomplete tender analysis; the provision must be read as a whole.
cases.holding: The Constitution Bench settled the interpretation of the lapse provision.
cases.relevance: Use for acquisition transition and lapse arguments.

cases.name: K.T. Plantation Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Karnataka
cases.facts: The Court considered compulsory acquisition and constitutional property protection.
cases.issue: What does Article 300A require when property is deprived by authority of law?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Deprivation must have authority of law and cannot be arbitrary; compensation principles remain relevant to constitutional review even though property is no longer a Fundamental Right.
cases.holding: The Court explained Article 300A and public-purpose review.

cases.name: Banda Development Authority v. Moti Lal Agarwal
cases.facts: Landowners challenged acquisition on delay, purpose and procedural grounds.
cases.issue: How should acquisition procedure and public purpose be scrutinised?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Courts examine statutory compliance and public purpose but do not substitute administrative planning judgment without a legal or constitutional defect.
cases.holding: The acquisition challenge was assessed under the statutory framework.
cases.relevance: Use for public purpose and judicial review.

enhancement.definition: Agricultural and urban land transfers use the same Transfer of Property Act unless a State law creates a special limit. Ceiling, tenancy and government-land restrictions are State statutes. They do not rewrite section 5.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Identify the Act that imposes the limit before applying a general transfer rule.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Transfer of Property Act, 1882; State land-reform statutes.
essentialIngredients: Permission if the State Act requires it
enhancement.detailedExplanation: A sale of agricultural land may need permission under a State tenancy or ceiling Act. Urban land may be affected by a development or ceiling statute. Those permissions are conditions of the State law. The deed is still a sale, mortgage, lease or gift under the Transfer of Property Act. Revenue records show possession and classification. They do not by themselves convey title.
enhancement.examples: A farmer sells agricultural land. The sale is section 54, and the State Act is checked for a restriction. A city plot uses the same sale section.
